title: Habit Sprint Constellation - micro-goal notebook
content:
Context and intention:
This is a lightweight, portable personal notebook for 2-week habit sprints. I wanted something less formal than an OKR doc but more structured than a random notes file — hence the "constellation" framing: 3–5 micro-goals are stars, each one gets 1–5 focus points (weight). The aim is to keep momentum while testing approaches that actually move team-level metrics (latency/cost/quality) without ballooning meetings.

How to use this page (my ritual):
- Monday morning: pick 3 stars (micro-goals) and assign focus points that sum to 8–10.
- End of day Friday: short reflection (2–3 lines) + one quantitative signal if available.
- Tag any blockers with links (Jira/PR/Slack) so I can turn them into tomorrow's quick task.
- Weekly experiment slot: 2 hours pure hacking on one micro-goal.

Current sprint (2025-02-10 → 2025-02-23)
Stars (micro-goals) and weights:
1) Small prompt suite for billing edge cases — 4 pts
   - deliverable: 8 test prompts + scoring rubric
   - why: flaky outputs are causing manual review; if we reduce false positives by 20% it saves ops time
   - linked: ENG-3421 (Linear), PR #1284
2) Prefix/KV-cache doclet for new model family — 3 pts
   - deliverable: internal MD + 30m demo to SRE
   - why: common customer use pattern is prefix-heavy; caching suggestion could cut per-token CPU by ~12%
3) Two micro-bench runs (fp16 vs q4_0) on toy workload — 2 pts
   - deliverable: a short table with latency/throughput/cost per 1k tokens
4) Habit: daily 15-minute inbox zero for open prompts/notes — 1 pt

Quant signals I’m watching this sprint:
- Time spent triaging prompts: target -30% vs last sprint (baseline ~3.5h/wk)
- Mean test pass rate on prompt suite: target 85%
- Measured per-token CPU for prefix-heavy synthetic workload: target -10%

Mid-sprint notes (2025-02-17)
- Prompt suite: drafted 5/8 prompts; two are ambiguous — need Aisha for content review (tagged in Slack thread).
- Cache doclet: started outline, but need data from infra (SLO traces). Linked artifact request sent (PR #1284 includes a trace snippet).
- Bench runs: initial fp16 run looks good; q4_0 had edge-case hallucination on instruction #3 — hypothesis: quantization + odd tokenization. TODO: reproduce with deterministic seed.

End-of-sprint reflection (2025-02-23)
Wins:
- Prompt suite at 8/8 and rubric baked, ran pilot with 2 reviewers; pass rate ~78% (below target). Good qualitative feedback on negative examples.
- Cache doclet MVP written; SRE asked for a short demo — demo scheduled for 2025-03-05.
- Bench runs delivered: fp16 latency 12% lower than q4_0 but q4_0 cost lower. Need a decision matrix for customers.

Learnings + next actions:
- Prompt suite needs better negative sampling — hypothesis: use longer negative prompts rather than truncated paraphrases. Next sprint: try 3 new negative templates and re-evaluate.
- Cache doclet should include an explicit mapping for common prefixes (system messages, auth tokens). Add that to checklist before demo.
- Quantization experiments need a deterministic harness — spin up small CI job (link to GH PR) to lock seeds.

Open questions / blockers:
- Who owns the canonical prompt examples for billing flows? (asked in Slack; waiting on reply from product).
- Does Dedicated infra already have prefix caching enabled for that model family? Need confirmation from infra team (pinged @infra).

Quick action list (for my TODO board):
- [ ] Add 3 negative templates to prompt suite (due 2025-03-02)
- [ ] Prototype deterministic bench harness (GH PR branch: bench/det-seed)
- [ ] Add prefix examples to doclet + screenshot traces (before 2025-03-05 demo)
- [ ] Convert pass/fail rubric to 0–3 scale and re-score (after new negatives)

Meta experiments (personal productivity):
- 15-minute inbox ritual seems to reduce context switching; will keep for now.
- Short batching of deep work (4x25m blocks) better than one 2-hour block when paired with scheduled micro-breaks.

Notes to future-me:
- If a micro-goal sits >2 sprints without progress, collapse it into a 1-hour spike then decide to drop.
- Resist the urge to over-index on metrics you can’t measure (focus on signals you can produce inside 2 weeks).

Quick links and artifacts referenced:
- Linear ENG-3421: prompt-benchmarks (priority: medium)
- GH PR 1284: infra traces and example configs
- Slack thread (prompt-reviews): timestamps and reviewer comments saved in thread

Random scratch ideas (unpolished):
- Constellation visualization: small SVG that maps stars to team-level metrics and shows a tiny heatmap of time spent. Could live in a small gist.
- Reward: when a sprint moves one star to "done" with measurable change, mark it on calendar (ritual helps).

End.
